newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl, happy with NATO-Russia deal, calls Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, happy with NATO-Russia deal, calls Yeltsin.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Thursday telephoned Russian President Boris Yeltsin to express satisfaction with a cooperation deal between NATO and Russia agreed on Wednesday.

Kohl and Yeltsin agreed in their assessment of the deal as a "fundamental, far-reaching step towards ensuring lasting stability and security in Europe", government spokesman Peter Hausmann said in a statement.

Kohl, a determined advocate of closer integration of Russia in Western institutions, also congratulated the two chief negotiators, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana.

The agreement, known as the NATO-Russia Founding Act, is intended to formalise Russian input into European security structures as NATO expands to include eastern European countries which used to be Russia's allies in the communist Warsaw Pact.
Hausmann said the agreement "opens up the prospect of long-term security partnership with Russia while defending the interests of the (NATO) alliance, including its future members, and of Russia".
The 16 NATO member governments must now approve the document, whose details have not yet been published, before a signing ceremony, pencilled in for May 27 in Paris.
